cards.front: What must a driver who is restricted to corrective lenses do during the road test?
cards.back: A driver restricted to corrective lenses must wear them during the road test.

cards.front: What happens if the vision exam shows you need lenses to see better?
cards.back: If the vision exam shows you need lenses to see better, you will be required to wear corrective lenses whenever you drive.

cards.front: What do you do after failing the vision exam, and when may you finish the test?
cards.back: Failing the vision exam means seeing a licensed eye specialist and returning the report to the examiner; if it shows you see well enough to drive safely, you may finish the test.

cards.front: How do the two corrective lens rules differ?
cards.back: Corrective lenses are required during the road test for drivers already restricted to them, and are required for all driving when the vision exam finds they are needed.

cards.front: What does the Alabama knowledge test ask about, and where do its questions come from?
cards.back: The knowledge test asks about Alabama traffic laws, road signs and safe-driving rules, and its questions come from this manual.

cards.front: When does a learner applicant get the learner license, and when does a regular applicant get the license?
cards.back: A learner-license applicant receives the learner license after passing the knowledge test and paying the fee, while a regular-license applicant receives the license after passing the road test and paying the fee.
cards.memory_hook: knowledge for learner, road for regular

cards.front: What must someone applying for both a motor driven cycle license and a learner license do?
cards.back: Someone applying for both a motor driven cycle license and a learner license must take both exams, and cycle or motorcycle applicants study the separate motorcycle manual.

cards.front: Who may use automated testing for the knowledge test?
cards.back: Automated testing is offered to every applicant who takes the knowledge test.

cards.front: Which test leads to the learner license, and which is the final step?
cards.back: The knowledge test leads to the learner license, while the road test is the final step that leads to the regular license.

cards.front: Who gives the road test, and who must come with a sixteen-year-old applicant?
cards.back: The road test, given by a driver license examiner, is the last step toward driving on public roads, and a sixteen-year-old applicant must come with a parent or guardian.

cards.front: What does the examiner check on the vehicle before the road test?
cards.back: Before the road test the examiner checks that the vehicle is safe and has brake lights, left and right turn signals, and a horn.

cards.front: What papers must you show for the road test, and when does a rental car qualify?
cards.back: You must show proof of insurance and registration for the road test, and a rental car qualifies only if you are named on the rental agreement as an additional driver.

decks.module: Tires, seating, medical review and ID cards

cards.front: How does the penny tread test tell you a tire is too worn?
cards.back: For the penny tread test, insert Lincoln's head first into the deepest groove; if his whole head shows, the tires are too worn to drive on and need replacing.

cards.front: How should you sit in the driver's seat, and why?
cards.back: Sit upright with your back against the seat and feet on the floor, because slouching can make the restraint system less effective.

cards.front: Where should your heel and the top of the steering wheel be?
cards.back: Keep your heel on the floor while your foot pivots between brake and accelerator, and set the steering wheel top no higher than your shoulders and below your chin.

cards.front: What may happen to a driver who seems to have an impairment that affects driving?
cards.back: A driver who seems to have an impairment affecting driving may need a physician's statement and periodic examiner checks, and failing to report the condition can lead to revocation.

cards.front: What does a non-driver ID card require, and who is it for?
cards.back: A non-driver ID card needs the same identity proof as a license and serves people who cannot physically qualify, hold no current Alabama license, or are giving up driving.

cards.front: How long is an Alabama license valid, and how early may you renew it?
cards.back: An Alabama license expires four years after issue and may be renewed any time within one hundred eighty days before the expiration date printed on it.

cards.front: Who may renew by mail, and what condition applies to their license?
cards.back: Military members and dependents, college students and others temporarily out of state for work may renew by mail if their photo-and-signature license was issued within the last four years.
cards.memory_hook: away from home, renew by mail

cards.front: What grace period does state law give after a license expires?
cards.back: State law gives a sixty-day grace period after expiration for renewal, and the license stays valid during that period.

cards.front: How long after expiring can a license be renewed without an exam, and from when does the new term run?
cards.back: A license can be renewed without an exam within three years after expiring, and the new license runs four years from the last expiration date, not from the issue date.

cards.front: May you drive on an expired license while you are still able to renew it?
cards.back: Although renewal stays possible up to three years after expiration, you may not legally drive on an expired license.

cards.front: How does the window before expiration differ from the window after it?
cards.back: The one hundred eighty-day window before expiration is for early renewal, while the sixty-day window after expiration is a grace period in which the license is still valid.

cards.front: What does the late-renewal window allow, and what does it not allow?
cards.back: Renewing without an exam is allowed up to three years after expiration, but that late-renewal window does not let you drive on the expired license.

cards.front: From what date does a normal renewal run compared with a late renewal?
cards.back: A normal renewal runs four years from issue, whereas a late renewal runs four years from the last expiration date.

cards.front: How do you replace an unexpired license that is lost, destroyed or unreadable?
cards.back: An unexpired license that is lost, destroyed or unreadable is replaced with a duplicate from the Probate Judge or License Commissioner, with no exam but with proof of identity such as a certified birth certificate.

cards.front: What can happen if you use a false affidavit to get a duplicate license?
cards.back: A false affidavit used to get a duplicate license can bring forgery or perjury charges, or both, punished by fine, prison or both.

cards.front: When do you get a duplicate instead of a renewal?
cards.back: A duplicate replaces an unexpired license that is lost, destroyed or unreadable, while a renewal replaces one that is expiring or expired.

decks.module: Changes to your license and license classes

cards.front: Who handles adding or removing classes, restrictions or endorsements, and are licenses forwarded?
cards.back: Adding, changing or removing classes, restrictions or endorsements requires a driver license examiner, and licenses and ID cards are never forwarded to another address.

cards.front: What do you need for a name change, and where must STAR ID holders make it?
cards.back: A name change needs documents such as a marriage certificate or court order with an updated Social Security card, and STAR ID holders must make it at an ALEA office.
cards.memory_hook: new name, new card, ALEA office

cards.front: How soon must you report a new Alabama address, and does it cost anything?
cards.back: After moving within Alabama you have thirty days to tell the Driver License Division your new address, which is updated on your record free of charge without reissuing the card.

cards.front: Which costs nothing, an address change or a corrected license after a name change?
cards.back: An address change within Alabama must be reported within thirty days and is free, while a corrected license after a name change carries a duplicate fee.

cards.front: What do Classes D, M and V cover?
cards.back: Class D covers generally all passenger vehicles not in Classes A, B, C or M; Class M covers motorcycles and motor-driven cycles, and Class V covers motorized watercraft.

cards.front: Which class is the ordinary passenger license, and which are for motorcycles and watercraft?
cards.back: Class D is the ordinary passenger-vehicle license, while Class M is for motorcycles and motor-driven cycles and Class V for motorized watercraft.
cards.memory_hook: D drives, M rides, V floats

cards.front: What vehicles need a Class A license?
cards.back: Class A is for combination vehicles with a combined weight rating over 26,000 pounds when the towed vehicle is rated over 10,000 pounds.

cards.front: What vehicles need Class B and Class C licenses?
cards.back: Class B is for single vehicles rated over 26,000 pounds towing no more than 10,000 pounds, and Class C is for vehicles built for sixteen or more people including the driver or placarded for hazardous materials.
cards.memory_hook: B heavy single, C sixteen riders

cards.front: What separates Class A from Class B when both involve heavy vehicles?
cards.back: Class A and Class B both involve vehicles rated over 26,000 pounds, but Class A applies when the towed vehicle is rated over 10,000 pounds and Class B when the tow is no more than that.

cards.front: Which lower classes may a Class A, B or C holder drive?
cards.back: Higher classes include lower ones: Class A holders may drive Class B, C and D vehicles, Class B holders Class C and D, and Class C holders Class D.

decks.module: Vessels, carrying your license and hands-free

cards.front: Who must be aboard when a young vessel licensee operates a vessel, and when may one operate alone?
cards.back: Anyone who turned twelve after January one, two thousand two and holds a vessel license may operate a vessel only with a licensed adult aged twenty-one or older aboard and ready to take control, though a licensed operator aged fourteen or older may operate alone.

cards.front: Who needs no vessel exam, and what must they still do?
cards.back: People born before April twenty-eight, one thousand nine hundred fifty-four need no vessel exam but must still visit a driver license office to have the vessel class issued.

cards.front: What must you carry while driving, and to whom must you show it?
cards.back: While driving you must carry the proper license or learner permit and show it to any law enforcement officer who asks.

cards.front: When does holding a wireless device break the Hands-Free Law?
cards.back: Under the Hands-Free Law effective June two thousand twenty-four, holding a wireless device is a violation when the driver is seen drifting across lanes without signaling, swerving, or otherwise driving improperly.

cards.front: What fines and points do hands-free convictions bring within twenty-four months?
cards.back: Within a twenty-four-month period, hands-free convictions cost a fifty dollars fine and one point the first time, one hundred dollars and two points the second, and one hundred fifty dollars and three points the third.

cards.front: What counts as a wireless device under the Hands-Free Law?
cards.back: For this law a wireless device means any device used to start or receive communication information or data.

cards.front: How do the second and third hands-free convictions compare with the first?
cards.back: A second hands-free conviction within twenty-four months doubles the first fine to one hundred dollars with two points, and a third brings one hundred fifty dollars with three points.

recap_hooks.text: Lens rules split two ways: wear them on the road test if restricted, and on every drive once the vision exam says so.
The knowledge test earns the learner license; the road test, with a safe car and your papers, is the final step.

recaps.module: Tires, seating, medical review and ID cards

recap_hooks.text: Check tread with a penny, sit upright with your heel down, and know that an ID card serves people who are not driving.
Renew up to one hundred eighty days early, keep a sixty-day grace period, and never drive on an expired license.
A late renewal runs from the old expiration date, and a duplicate replaces a license that is lost, not expiring.

recaps.module: Changes to your license and license classes

recap_hooks.text: Report a new address within thirty days for free; a name change needs documents and a corrected license.
Class D is the everyday license, Class A and Class B cover heavy vehicles, and higher classes include lower ones.

recap_hooks.text: Show your license when an officer asks, and remember that holding a phone while driving badly brings rising fines and points.
